title: Sun Memory
concept: Putting all the tools down on purpose, so you can be together without improving anything. It’s meant to become a few easy hours you’ll both remember, like a warm afternoon. Quick is a few minutes; Full is 2 to 24 hours.
whenToUse: When talk about the tools is crowding out the ease between you, a heavy stretch of repair has just ended, or the rituals have started to feel like a chore list. Try Quick first.
steps: Either of you can call it, and either of you can end it early. No reason is needed.
All system-talk stops straight away: no talk about the tools, the reviews or how you could do this better.
Pick a length. Quick: a few minutes inside one ritual. Full: 2 to 24 hours.
Do something easy together: a walk, a meal, music, a long hug if it’s welcome. No debrief.
When it ends, don’t go back over it. Keep any follow-up practical and kind.

phrases.text: Can we call a Quick Sun Memory?

working: Halfway through making dinner, A calls a Quick Sun Memory. B puts a song on, they sing along badly, and for three minutes nothing needs sorting. Afterwards B only asks, “What shall we have for dinner tomorrow?”
notWorking: B calls one every time the Weekly Reset comes round, to dodge a talk A needs. A rest that keeps landing on the same hard conversation has stopped being rest. Book that talk outside the window.
activity: Agree one phrase for calling a Quick Sun Memory and a short list of easy things to do. Try one this week.
warn: It pauses talk about the tools only. Safety, childcare, logistics and any repair you’ve already booked carry on. Either of you can end it early, for any reason. Naming a safety concern ends it at once.
note: Calling one every week? Change the rituals at the monthly part of your Weekly Reset instead of pausing them again and again.
